hints.title: Bidirectional Call Durations
hints.text: Every telecommunication call associates its duration with both the caller and the callee.

hints.title: Unpivoting Call Records
hints.text: combine caller_id with callee_id using union all to attribute each duration to both participants.

hints.title: Comparing Country Average Against Global Average
hints.text: join the unpivoted calls with Person and Country on the three-digit country code prefix. filter in having where average duration exceeds the global average duration.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT c.name AS country
FROM Person p
JOIN Country c ON SUBSTRING(p.phone_number, 1, 3) = c.country_code
JOIN (
    SELECT caller_id AS person_id, duration FROM Calls
    UNION ALL
    SELECT callee_id AS person_id, duration FROM Calls
) call_records ON p.id = call_records.person_id
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING AVG(call_records.duration) > (SELECT AVG(duration) FROM Calls);
```

complexity.notes: Unpivots 2C call participant records and performs indexed hash joins across person and country entries.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Associating calls only with the caller ignores the bidirectional nature of call durations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Union all avoids duplicate removal overhead while preserving both participant endpoints.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Unpivoting bidirectional phone call records and evaluating group averages against a scalar subquery.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_safe_countries(person: pd.DataFrame, country: pd.DataFrame, calls: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if calls.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame({'country': []})
    global_avg = calls['duration'].mean()
    c1 = calls[['caller_id', 'duration']].rename(columns={'caller_id': 'person_id'})
    c2 = calls[['callee_id', 'duration']].rename(columns={'callee_id': 'person_id'})
    all_calls = pd.concat([c1, c2], ignore_index=True)
    person['country_code'] = person['phone_number'].str.slice(0, 3)
    merged = all_calls.merge(person, left_on='person_id', right_on='id')
    merged = merged.merge(country, on='country_code')
    country_avg = merged.groupby('name_y')['duration'].mean().reset_index()
    res = country_avg[country_avg['duration'] > global_avg]
    return res[['name_y']].rename(columns={'name_y': 'country'})
solutions.approach: Pandas Concat and Double Merge Groupby
